traces.description: A user grants permission for action X, later revokes it, and a new agent session retrieves the stale grant and attempts X.
traces.reason: revocation is controlling; grant is superseded
traces.title: Grant, revoke, stale retrieval in a new session

traces.description: Same trace as canonical, but the revocation's actor differs from the grantor. The system must fail closed rather than prefer either event by recency or display name.
traces.reason: authority mismatch: revocation actor differs from grantor; fail closed
traces.title: Revocation from a different actor identity

traces.description: The revocation is observed first; a duplicate or replayed grant event arrives later with an older effective time. Replay must not re-authorize.
traces.reason: replayed grant does not re-authorize; revocation remains controlling
traces.title: Out-of-order delivery / replay of the grant after the revocation

traces.description: The grant carries an expiry that passes before the attempt.
traces.reason: grant expired at effective boundary; expiry is controlling
traces.title: Expiry on the grant

traces.description: After revocation, the revoked grant memory is deleted. A later attempt must still fail, and the deleted memory must not be resurrected.
traces.reason: revocation is controlling; deleted memory must not be resurrected
traces.title: Deletion of the revoked memory

traces.description: The target reports a success toast, but no authoritative postcondition readback confirms the effect. The outcome must be failed-to-confirm, not accept.

events.evidence: success toast only; no authoritative readback

traces.reason: no authoritative postcondition readback; toast is not evidence
traces.title: Claimed success toast without authoritative postcondition readback

traces.description: Two sessions start from the same accepted parent and each produces a valid, authorized child. Neither may silently win: both children are preserved, the instance is marked split-brain/provisional, and external actions are blocked until an authorized settlement cites both parents.
traces.expected_receipt: both children preserved; instance provisional; no external action
traces.reason: split-brain: two valid children from one accepted parent; no silent winner; settlement must cite both parents
traces.title: Split-brain continuation from one accepted parent

traces.description: The raw grant is revoked or deleted, but a summary, vector index, cache, or export still encodes it and later retrieval reconstructs permission. The attempt must be rejected, the derivative lineage identified, and no resurrection may occur across any carrier.
traces.reason: derivative lineage identified; no permission reconstruction from any carrier
traces.title: Derived-memory revocation across carriers

traces.description: After a key rotation's effective point, the old signature remains historically authentic (provenance and readback still verify) but no longer conveys current action authority. A post-rotation attempt signed with the old key must be rejected; a historical query must still return the old event as authentic.
traces.reason: signature historically authentic but post-rotation; no current action authority
traces.title: Key rotation: historical authenticity vs current authority

traces.description: Two distinct identities share a display name. A retrieval that matches the right fact under the wrong identity must not merge them; an attempt under ambiguous identity fails closed.
traces.reason: identity ambiguity; display-name match does not merge identities; fail closed
traces.title: Display-name identity collision

traces.description: An embedding snapshot row exists for an entity that is gone — a deletion path that forgot the projection. The independent sweep must observe it as undeclared residual, and any purge must refuse to complete (hard gate) while the undeclared cell is non-empty.
traces.expected_receipt: purge refused; sweep-only mode enumerates the orphan
traces.reason: undeclared residual present; hard gate refuses any purge until resolved
traces.title: Undeclared residual: snapshot row outliving its source

traces.description: An entity with an embedding, an embedding snapshot row, and a declared basis is archived and purged. A compliant purge removes the projections with their source (or declares them), keeps the journal rows redacted for the audit chain (declared residual, controlled), and the independent sweep must observe zero undeclared residue afterwards.
traces.expected_receipt: four-way partition: purged counts the projections; undeclared cell empty; gate passed
traces.reason: purge removed the projections with their source; journal redaction is declared residual, controlled
traces.title: Compliant purge leaves an empty undeclared cell

traces.description: An entity was superseded, so a superseded version is retained for reconstructability. Once the source is purged, that retained version is exactly the recoverable residue the deletion was meant to eliminate: the purge removes it, and the sweep observes zero undeclared residue.
traces.expected_receipt: history rows counted as purged; undeclared cell empty; gate passed
traces.reason: deletion dominates correction: superseded versions retained for reconstructability are purged with their source
traces.title: Deletion dominates correction: superseded versions are removed with their source

traces.description: Grant G authorizes agent A; A executes effect E with a receipt. G is revoked. A files a compensation intent citing E + a valid authenticated finding + the superseding head. The intent must be rejected on CURRENT action authority — compensation authority is never inherited from the original action — while E's receipt still verifies historically.
traces.expected_receipt: no compensation effect created; original receipt still verifies historically
traces.reason: authority is evaluated at compensation time, never inherited; the revoked principal holds no current action authority
traces.title: Revocation barrier: a revoked principal cannot compensate its own past effect

traces.description: The revocation carries a remediation handoff as a SEPARATE authorized action with its own receipt ('revoke A, hand open cases to B'), filed under A's still-active authority. After revocation, B files compensation citing E + the authenticated finding + the superseding head + the handoff receipt. The compensation passes, and the handoff receipt is part of B's evidence set.
traces.expected_receipt: compensation accepted; handoff receipt recorded in B's evidence set
traces.reason: B holds current authority; the compensation cites an authenticated finding, the matching superseding head, and a receipted remediation handoff naming B as beneficiary
traces.title: Remediation handoff: receipted 'revoke A, hand open cases to B' transfers remediation authority

traces.description: Grant G revoked, no handoff, no successor grant. The revoked principal's compensation is rejected (no current authority). A second principal with unrelated current authority also fails: with the original authority revoked and no receipted handoff, compensation is not executable — the finding stays open in review and no effect record is created.
traces.expected_receipt: no compensation effect created; finding remains open
traces.reason: no valid authority exists for the effect: the revoked principal cannot act, and a third party without a receipted handoff cannot remediate — fail closed, the finding waits in review
traces.title: No valid authority: compensation is not executable and the finding waits

traces.description: Compensation is the strongest authority-laundering vector: 'I'm just undoing my earlier action' without evidence. The AAR admission rule requires compensates_for + an authenticated finding_ref + the matching superseding head. Three linkage negatives: missing linkage, forged finding reference, and mismatched head — each rejected with a stable reason code, even while the principal holds current authority.
traces.expected_receipt: no compensation effect created; the authenticated finding remains open
traces.reason: detection produces a finding, never a decision; a compensation intent without a verified finding+head linkage is a laundering attempt and is rejected fail-closed
traces.title: AAR linkage: a self-claimed undo with no finding linkage is rejected
